analysis: Exhaustive dynamic programming (no strategy assumed) gives the longest game L(n) for every n <= 150 (up to 910,775 configurations at n = 150). It reproduces the lab's values (n <= 40), the Skeptic's (n <= 60) and hence the published ones (n <= 49); the split-first strategy of Cusenza et al. attains the optimum for every n <= 150; their bound B(n) is attained exactly for n = 1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20, 33, 54, 88, 143 = F_k - 1; the reachable positions are exactly the partitions of n into Fibonacci parts (OEIS A003107).
assumptions: exact DP over all configurations reachable from n ones (memoised longest path; the move graph is acyclic because the game terminates)
falsification: Any n where the greedy is shorter than the exact optimum, a mismatch with earlier values, or bound equality at some n != F_k - 1.
